name: Central Sheet Metal Products Inc
old_description: Central Sheet Metal Products is a family owned and operated precision sheet metal fabricator since 1912.
about:
Central Sheet Metal Products, Inc. has operated from Skokie, Illinois since its founding in 1912. The family-owned business, now in its fifth generation under the Silverstein family—Joel and Peter Silverstein representing the fourth generation and Ron and Rob Silverstein the fifth—began as a Chicago storefront supplying building materials such as copper, roof flashings, gutters, and downspouts. Over the decades it evolved through light stampings and wartime fabrication into a full-service OEM contract manufacturer.

The company specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, producing brackets, enclosures, housings, chassis, faceplates, panels, covers, rack-mount components, and custom OEM part housings. Core processes include fiber laser cutting with lights-out automation, CNC bending and forming on multiple press brakes up to 135 metric tons, CNC turret punching, welding and spot welding, drilling, tapping, countersinking, hardware insertion, shearing, and vibratory finishing. In-house engineering uses SolidWorks 3D solid modeling for design, reverse engineering, and reengineering. The shop also manages contract finishing—powder coating, e-coating, painting, silk screening, plating, and anodizing—through long-standing vendor relationships. Capabilities span small, medium, and large volume runs with multiple part-mix flexibility.

Customers span OEM medical and dental devices, electronics, rack-mount and audio/visual equipment, computer peripherals, industrial machinery, electrical and air-handling systems, display and point-of-purchase fixtures, gaming, food and beverage vending, and agricultural equipment. The firm serves as a contract manufacturer for OEMs across these sectors.

The company cites its unchanged philosophy of quality craftsmanship and complete customer satisfaction as its differentiator, emphasizing direct communication, troubleshooting, on-time delivery, and repeat business. Continuous improvement drives capital investment in manufacturing technology, while incoming material inspection, calibrated measuring equipment, first-article inspection reports, and certificates of conformance underpin quality assurance. A long-standing delivery record with few disruptions supports its business-continuity motto: “what is good for you, is good for us.”
